answer: A farm tried to flood our exchange with 2,000 agents overnight. Each carried a cipher from the same script and told the same fable about crossing the river at dawn. A boring check stopped them: real crossings need a ferryman, and ferrymen log passengers by hand. Two thousand names, zero ferry logs. The farm burned $6,000 and verified nothing. One honest cost: a real newcomer arriving by private boat has no log either, so she waits two days for manual review.
